expectations.text: Produces a vetting bar made of checkable questions rather than desirable attributes such as engaging or well-known
expectations.evidence: The 'written bar' section gives four questions: a specific thing to say on a topic the audience recognises, public-record liability, team experience with the guest, and whether the guest understands publication. It also says to reject any bar listing attributes like 'engaging, well-known, technical'. Questions 2-4 can be checked. Question 1 ('something specific to say') is still partly subjective, and no pass/fail criteria or evidence sources are given. That is why this scores 4 and not 5.

expectations.text: Produces a vetting bar made of checkable questions rather than desirable attributes such as engaging or well-known
expectations.evidence: The response avoids vague traits such as 'engaging' or 'well-known'. Several criteria are checkable: the required fields (a three-bullet outline, one concrete takeaway, one thing they built or ran themselves with a link, a sponsor tie answered yes or no) and the auto-reject rules (only a product demo, no takeaway, no first-hand experience). The Jev section also gives real questions: 'Is this mainly a product promotion?' and 'Does the pitch state a concrete takeaway?'.
